concepts.def: Course in General Linguistics 1916; signifier and signified arbitrarily linked; basis for semiotic analysis of image.
Charles Sanders Peirce (1839-1914); icon (resemblance), index (causal), symbol (convention); applied to photography by Rosalind Krauss 1977.
Rhetoric of the Image 1964 analysed Panzani ad; denotation vs connotation; Mythologies 1957 popularised semiotic critique.
Gillian Rose's Visual Methodologies 2001 systematised four sites (production, image, audiencing, circulation) and three modalities.
Reading Images 1996 grammar of visual design; represented and interactive meanings; vectors, gaze, framing.
W J T Mitchell's Picture Theory 1994; pictorial turn; image as agent rather than passive sign.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Communicating Visual Arts — a core area of Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Communicating Visual Arts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Communicating Visual Arts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
